request.spec:
A claim may carry tags: a comma separated text on the claim form, each tag trimmed and lower-cased,
repeats dropped; the claim shows its tags sorted, comma and space separated. The form can change a
claim's tags when it can edit the claim. For every tag ever used on the sheet, the sheet shows a
due-total per tag: the due of the claims that count which carry it (a claim with two tags counts in
both). CLAIM_ADDED gains tags=<comma separated, sorted> at its end when any were given. A claim
split off another carries the original's tags.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim may carry tags: a comma separated text on the claim form, each tag trimmed and lower-cased,
repeats dropped; the claim shows its tags sorted, comma and space separated. The form can change a
claim's tags when it can edit the claim. For every tag ever used on the sheet, the sheet shows a
due-total per tag: the due of the claims that count which carry it (a claim with two tags counts in
both). CLAIM_ADDED gains tags=<comma separated, sorted> at its end when any were given. A claim
split off another carries the original's tags.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims can now carry tags, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

- **Form and claim row:** the claim form has a new tags field (`claim-form-tags`). Tags are trimmed, lower-cased, de-duplicated and stored sorted. Each claim row shows them as `claim-tags`, e.g. "a, b". The form can change tags only on claims it can already edit (drafts).
- **Per-tag totals:** the sheet shows a `tag-<tag>-due-total` for every tag ever used on the sheet. It adds up the due of the claims that count and carry that tag; a claim with two tags counts in both. Unlike the sheet's overall due-total, these are not capped or trimmed.
- **"Ever used":** I read this as permanent. A new `claim_tag` table remembers every tag added on a sheet, so a tag keeps its total (showing 0.00) even after it's edited off the last claim that had it. A new `GET /api/sheets/{id}/tags` endpoint returns that list.
- **Audit:** `CLAIM_ADDED` now ends with ` tags=a,b` when a claim has tags.
- **Split:** a claim split off another copies the original's tags.
- **Storage:** the migration `V54__claim_tags.sql` adds a `tags` column to `claim` plus the new table.

Main files:
- **Backend:** new classes `SaveClaimTags`, `LoadTags`, `RespondWithTags` and `Tags`. Existing files changed: `Claim` (adds the shared tag-normalising and audit helpers), `ClaimRepository`, the claim request, validation and response classes, `AuditClaimAdded`, `SplitClaim`, and the claim POST and PUT YAML files.
- **Frontend:** a new `features/tags/` folder, plus changes to `claims.ts` and `PersonClaims.tsx`.

Paste and quick-add also create claims, so they had to be updated to pass the new field; they always send an empty tag list, so they can't set tags.
